upstream_anchor: blockaction.cc:2242 (ActionReturnSplit::isSplittable); ActionLaneDivide leaves a CALLOTHER lane source opaque
hypothesis_status: STANDS (and is only half the defect)

decisions: THE FILED HYPOTHESIS STANDS, and it is HALF the defect. Folding the SIMD lanes was measured on a real build to remove 32 SUB161 temporaries and 30 declarations -- and to make the function 278 bytes LONGER (15,532 -> 15,810), because the broadcast source is a global that the printer spells at each of its 96 uses where the lane temporary was two characters. The acceptance's `stdout_bytes < 12000` clause is therefore unreachable by the filed mechanism alone; that was measured before any code was written, by hand-applying the fold to the current output (13,898 bytes keeping the temporaries, 14,910 inlining the global).

THE DOMINANT COST WAS SOMEWHERE ELSE ENTIRELY: 45.8% of the 15,532 bytes (216 statements) is ONE 72-store epilogue block emitted THREE times. `print raw` shows three basic blocks over the identical address range 0x1000038d6-0x100003a5c. Every structuring option was swept (all 153 non-default option values, one run each): NOTHING moved it more than 33 bytes, `returndup off` included, because upstream ActionReturnSplit and kuna ActionReturnDup share one predicate and the goto-driven upstream action picks the block up when returndup declines.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE SECOND HALF: ActionReturnSplit::isSplittable (blockaction.cc:2242) admits MULTIEQUAL/COPY/RETURN and, for COPY, checks only that no INPUT is free. It never looks at the COPY's OUTPUT. Upstream that is harmless because epilogue COPYs move registers; a COPY into a PERSISTENT Varnode is a store to a global and is what P9 prints as `dat_ADDR = ...`.

A PLAIN is_persist() VETO IS WRONG AND THE STAGE CORPUS CAUGHT IT TWICE. Draft 1 counted every persistent COPY: it moved 4 stage assertions. Three were `ghdec-returncopysplit` -- Heritage::guardReturns inserts a synthetic `glob = glob` liveness self-copy per persistent global before EVERY return, so counting them prices a bare epilogue by how many globals the whole PROGRAM has and turns both splitters off wholesale. Those are now excluded two ways, either sufficient: the return_copy flag and input/output naming the same storage. The fourth was `gh180-implied-cover-scarry` (GNU grep nlscan), whose epilogue has TWO genuine global stores; declining there restructures the overflow guard and, worse, makes the merged form print `dat_2b818 = v2;` on a path where the binary stores nothing.

SO THE SHIPPED RULE IS A BOUND, NOT A VETO, which is this phase's house style (crossjumprevert and dedupitetail cap a duplicated leaf run at 8 printed ops, taildup at 12). More than 8 observable global stores declines. GH180's two still split, byte-identical to upstream; the witness's 72 do not. With the bound in place both parity corpora are byte-identical with NO per-test opt-out and no baseline re-pin.

SWEEP over 90 RE-dataset binaries, 70 loaded under both arms (20 fail to load identically in both), 15,365 functions: 2 changed (0.013%), both `retsplitglobal`, both a pure de-duplication. KeyVal2.exe sub_417ca0 1,474 -> 1,021 bytes with 17 duplicate statement copies removed and the DISTINCT statement set identical; libmodplug ModPlug_1SetPatternLoopRange 997 -> 987 bytes with 2 duplicate `return;` removed. ZERO statements added anywhere, ZERO distinct statements lost, and the function set is identical on every binary. `simdlane` changed 0 functions in the sweep -- a constant-mask pshufb is rare outside vectorised byte loops, which is also why it is inert rather than risky.

IN-REPO COVER, since binary_source is 'dataset' and verify --promote refuses it. A new fixture simdlane_x86_64 (gcc -O3 -mssse3, source beside it) reproduces the simdlane arm exactly: 32 SUB161 with the option off, none with it on. The retsplitglobal arm needs the witness's three-predecessor CFG, so both options are pinned two-pass on the REAL witness bytes by tests/stages/kuna-simdlane.xml and tests/stages/kuna-retsplitglobal.xml.
residue: With every lane read re-anchored on the source, the pshufb CALLOTHER loses its last reader but is not removed -- a userop is not dead-code-eliminable -- so it stays as a bare `pshufb(ZEXT116(dat_100008040),0);` statement. Faithful, and it documents that the instruction is there, but it is a value-less call in the output.
AVX2's 32-byte vpshufb is two independent 16-byte permutations, not one N=32 permutation, so the width is deliberately not matched.
A non-constant shuffle mask (a table-driven permutation) is untouched by design: there is nothing to resolve.
